questions.q: What will happen if Israel returns to Yahweh?
questions.a: The nations will ask Yahweh to bless them, and they will praise him.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the people of Judah and Jerusalem to do before he speaks to them?
questions.a: He tells them to prepare their hearts to receive his message.

questions.q: What will happen because of the people’s wickedness?
questions.a: Because of his anger with them, Yahweh will bring disaster to them from the north.

questions.q: What will the lion do to the people?
questions.a: He will destroy their cities.

questions.q: Why would the people wrap themselves in sackcloth?
questions.a: They would do it to show that they were sorry for their sins.

questions.q: What will happen to the king, the officials, the priests, and the prophets when Yahweh punishes the people?
questions.a: They will all be very afraid and terrified.

questions.q: Why does Jeremiah think Yahweh has deceived the people?
questions.a: Yahweh had told the people there would be peace, but now their enemies are about to attack them with swords.

questions.q: What will the army that attacks Judah be like?
questions.a: It will be like a hot wind from the desert, not a gentle breeze.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to the people?
questions.a: He says he will punish them.

questions.q: What are the enemy’s horses like?
questions.a: They are faster than eagles.

questions.q: How can the people of Jerusalem be saved?
questions.a: They must cleanse their hearts from wickedness.

questions.q: From where do the messengers announce that disaster is coming from?
questions.a: From Dan and the hills of Ephraim.

questions.q: Why are the enemy soldiers coming from a distant land?
questions.a: They are coming because Judah has rebelled against Yahweh.

questions.q: What is causing these troubles to happen to the people?
questions.a: Their own conduct and evil deeds are causing these troubles.

questions.q: Why is Jeremiah in anguish?
questions.a: He hears the sound of the horn, an alarm for battle.

questions.q: What will happen to the land?
questions.a: Disaster after disaster will come until the whole land is ruined.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah continue to see and hear during the battle?
questions.a: He continues to see the battle flags and hear the sound of the trumpets.

questions.q: What is the foolishness of the people?
questions.a: They do not know Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah see in his vision about the land?
questions.a: He saw that the land was empty and had no form, and there was no light in the sky.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah see the mountains and hills doing in his vision?
questions.a: He saw them shaking and quaking.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah see was missing from the land in his vision?
questions.a: He saw that there were no people and that all the birds had flown away.

questions.q: Why was the land that Jeremiah saw empty?
questions.a: The land was empty because Yahweh was angry.

questions.q: How completely will Yahweh destroy the land?
questions.a: He will ruin the whole land, but he will not destroy it completely.

questions.q: What will happen to the land and the sky because of Yahweh’s plan?
questions.a: The land will mourn, and the sky will become dark.

questions.q: What will the people in every city do?
questions.a: They will run away from the attackers and leave the cities empty.

questions.q: What does Jerusalem wear to try to look attractive?
questions.a: She wears scarlet clothing, gold jewelry, and eye paint.

questions.q: What does the daughter of Zion say about the murderers who are coming?
questions.a: She says she is afraid because murderers are about to kill her.

commentary.text: Exhortations and promises. (Jer. 4:1-2) Judah exhorted to repentance. (Jer. 4:3-4) Judgements denounced. (Jer. 4:5-18) The approaching ruin of Judah. (Jer. 4:19-31)
Jer. 4:1,2 The first two verses should be read with the last chapter. Sin must be put away out of the heart, else it is not put away out of God's sight, for the heart is open before him.

Jer. 4:3,4 An unhumbled heart is like ground untilled. It is ground which may be improved; it is our ground let out to us; but it is fallow; it is over-grown with thorns and weeds, the natural product of the corrupt heart. Let us entreat the Lord to create in us a clean heart, and to renew a right spirit within us; for except a man be born again, he cannot enter into the kingdom of heaven.

Jer. 4:5-18 The fierce conqueror of the neighbouring nations was to make Judah desolate. The prophet was afflicted to see the people lulled into security by false prophets. The approach of the enemy is described. Some attention was paid in Jerusalem to outward reformation; but it was necessary that their hearts should be washed, in the exercise of true repentance and faith, from the love and pollution of sin. When lesser calamities do not rouse sinners and reform nations, sentence will be given against them. The Lord's voice declares that misery is approaching, especially against wicked professors of the gospel; when it overtakes them, it will be plainly seen that the fruit of wickedness is bitter, and the end is fatal.

Jer. 4:19-31 The prophet had no pleasure in delivering messages of wrath. He is shown in a vision the whole land in confusion. Compared with what it was, every thing is out of order; but the ruin of the Jewish nation would not be final. Every end of our comforts is not a full end. Though the Lord may correct his people very severely, yet he will not cast them off. Ornaments and false colouring would be of no avail. No outward privileges or profession, no contrivances would prevent destruction. How wretched the state of those who are like foolish children in the concerns of their souls! Whatever we are ignorant of, may the Lord make of good understanding in the ways of godliness. As sin will find out the sinner, so sorrow will, sooner or later, find out the secure.
